metric_definitions.get_count: GET observations in DuckDB HTTP logs, reconciled with the independent server
metric_definitions.head_count: HEAD observations; HEAD contributes zero body bytes
metric_definitions.server_written_bytes: Sum of bytes successfully written by the independent server to streams
metric_definitions.requested_range_bytes: Sum of resolved GET request Range lengths
metric_definitions.confirmed_range_bytes: Sum of GET response interval lengths confirmed by response headers
metric_definitions.declared_body_bytes: Sum of GET Content-Length; HEAD contributes zero
metric_definitions.unique_coverage_bytes: Length of union of confirmed GET response intervals
metric_definitions.repeated_coverage_bytes: Sum of confirmed interval lengths minus their union, not assumed waste
metric_definitions.coverage: Union of confirmed GET response intervals, half-open byte offsets
metric_definitions.totals_scope: Complete or observed subset; only complete reconciled runs enter successful runs
metric_definitions.query_duration_ms: SELECT execution through full result consumption; excludes input binding
metric_definitions.elapsed_ms: Worker startup, binding, execution and cleanup; excludes metadata preparation

limitations: Premeasured loopback HTTP captures; static browsing executes no SQL.
Fresh worker and disabled external file cache; OS/disk caches are uncontrolled, not cold S3.
Server writes do not prove client receipt, chunk decoding or use. Overlap is not automatic waste.
Read bytes do not imply proportional speedup, S3 performance or a cloud bill.
One workload on one month does not establish a universally better layout.
A/B change writer, encoding and layout as well as row groups; no single-factor attribution.
B/C use identical writer settings; row order is the intended difference. Ties have no extra key.
Pruning and sorting are established mechanisms; ParquetScope exposes this workload's observations.
Captures retain SQL, column names and metadata; they omit preview rows, not all possible data.
Versions, scheduling and platform can affect sizes, timing and request sequences.
Runs are sequential A1..A3, B1..B3, C1..C3, without cache eviction or randomized timing trials.
